preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to configure burn settings or call manual burn
LP burn must be enabled (lpBurnEnabled = true)
Sufficient time must pass since last burn (block.timestamp >= lastLpBurnTime + lpBurnFrequency for auto, or block.timestamp > lastManualLpBurnTime + manualBurnFrequency for manual)
UniswapV2 pair must hold MARVIN token balance to burn

logic_check.expected_value: LP pair MARVIN token balance decreased after burn execution

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, call setAutoLPBurnSettings to configure burn frequency (minimum 600 seconds) and burn percentage (maximum 1000 = 10%). Wait for lpBurnFrequency to elapse, then trigger any transfer to the automatedMarketMakerPairs[to] to execute autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() automatically. Alternatively, call manualBurnLiquidityPairTokens(uint256 percent) directly with up to 10% burn after 30 minute cooldown. This burns MARVIN tokens from the liquidity pool to 0xdead address, reducing pool liquidity and manipulating token economics without liquidity provider consent.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The MarvinInu contract has an automatic LP token burn feature that can be configured by the owner. When enabled, transfers to automated market maker pairs trigger autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() which burns MARVIN tokens from the LP pair to 0xdead. The owner can set burn frequency (min 600s) and burn percentage (max 10% = 1000 basis points). This allows the owner to manipulate token economics by reducing LP liquidity without LP provider consent.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(). 2. Configure auto LP burn with minimum frequency (600s) and maximum percentage (1000 = 10%). 3. Enable trading to initialize lastLpBurnTime. 4. Warp time forward to exceed the burn frequency. 5. Transfer tokens from a non-excluded address to the AMM pair to trigger auto burn. 6. Verify the LP pair balance decreased.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get contract instance and read uniswapV2Pair address. 2. Record initial LP balance. 3. vm.prank(owner) to impersonate owner. 4. Call setAutoLPBurnSettings(600, 1000, true). 5. Call enableTrading(). 6. vm.warp(block.timestamp + 601) to pass burn frequency. 7. Transfer tokens from attacker (non-excluded) to uniswapV2Pair. 8. Assert LP balance decreased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: Since ownership is renounced, we cannot call owner-only functions like enableTrading() or setAutoLPBurnSettings(). However, if trading was already enabled before renouncement and auto-burn settings were already configured, we can still trigger the auto-burn mechanism by executing sell transactions.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Check current contract state (tradingActive, lpBurnEnabled, lpBurnFrequency, percentForLPBurn). 2. If trading is active and auto-burn is enabled, acquire tokens and execute sell transactions to trigger burns. 3. Profit from deflationary effect as supply decreases.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Read contract state to see if trading is active and auto-burn is enabled. 2. If not, we need to find another approach (maybe the vulnerability is that anyone can trigger burns under certain conditions). 3. Acquire MARVIN tokens (use deal() if possible). 4. Execute sell transactions to trigger auto-burn. 5. Verify that burns occur and attacker profits.
attempts.failure_reflection: The owner address is zero (0x000...000), which means ownership was renounced. We cannot impersonate the zero address to call owner-only functions. Need to check if trading is already enabled and if auto-burn is already configured.
